## Changes
- One window, the **AFC console**, now holds every AFC feature. It replaces the guidance panel, the Maneuver Tools window and the AFC additions to the stock Transfer Planner. **F4** and **View > Transfer Planner** open it, and so does the new **AFC** menu in the top bar. The stock Transfer Planner stays as the game ships it and is one click away from the **TRANSFER** page. Switch **F4 OPENS AFC** off to give F4 back to the stock planner. ([#127](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-AdvancedFlightComputer/pull/127))
- The console has seven pages in the order of a mission: **LAUNCH**, **MANEUVER**, **TRANSFER**, **BURNS**, **LAND**, **STAGING** and **TUNE**. Each page shows its picture first (the climb profile, the orbit sketch, the porkchop plot, the descent profile), then its inputs, and one button at the bottom commits the action that fits where the craft is now.
- The head of the console always says where the craft is and who flies it (AFC, stock AUTO, both, or you), and holds the one stop for what runs. A real failure shows as one red band under the altitude counter, also with the console closed, until you press **OK**.
- You can size the window, switch to a **WIDE** layout with the picture at the left, and the console remembers its page, size and position. It stops above the stock burn and autopilot panels.
- **LAND** puts every way down on one page: **DEORBIT**, **BOOSTBACK**, **LAND NOW** and **HOVER**, with a table that shows how each solver lands and what it suits. While a deorbit waits or flies, the settings that it reads are locked, and the lock reason is on the row.
- **TUNE** holds the tuning values of every guidance mode. A changed value shows its default and a **RESET**, and each set shows the count of its changed values.
- **LAUNCH** lets the ascent plan choose its own lift-off time or LAN, and sizes the booster reserve and the landing site of each returnable stage. A booster that must fly a long way back now gets a plannable boostback burn and a faster flip. These controls were added to the previous guidance panel and now live on the console. ([#122](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-AdvancedFlightComputer/pull/122) to [#126](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-AdvancedFlightComputer/pull/126))
- Fixed: a G-FOLD deorbit with **MEASURE COM ABOVE LEGS** on stopped by itself with "The deorbit settings or control switches changed", because the measured vehicle height changes while propellant drains. The deorbit now keeps the height it was planned with. ([#128](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-AdvancedFlightComputer/pull/128))
- Fixed: after a failed climb plan, the convex ascent could retry at a Max q above what KSA allows and fly a plan that breaks the vehicle up. The retry is now capped at 195 kPa, a plan that peaks at 196 kPa or more is refused with the reason, and the Max q field stops at 195 kPa. The default is 195 kPa. ([#129](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-AdvancedFlightComputer/pull/129))
- Guidance itself does not change. The console moves and renames the controls and shows more of what the solvers already know, and the headless test suite gives the same numbers as before.
